steps.name: prompt
steps.text: Write the introduction for our paper on MMICL, a vision-language model trained for multi-modal in-context learning. Explain why current VLMs struggle with prompts containing multiple images, lay out the specific limitations, and summarize our approach, dataset and main results.

steps.name: skeleton_outline
steps.text:
- VLMs progress, but weak on complex multi-modal prompts with multiple images
- Limitation 1: text-to-image reference
- Limitation 2: relationships between multiple images
- Limitation 3: learning from in-context multi-modal demonstrations
- Our contributions: MMICL, context scheme, dataset
- Results

steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
- VLMs progress, but weak on complex multi-modal prompts with multiple images
  - general-purpose VLMs: big advances; mostly LLM + visual encoder; good zero-shot on visual tasks
  - LLMs extract background knowledge/task info from prompt via ICL; most VLMs can't handle complex prompts with multiple images
  - previous studies: user queries with a single image, not interleaved images + text
  - Flamingo, Kosmos-1 handle multiple images, but pre-training data = interleaved image-text crawled from web
  - gap between pre-training prompts and real user queries (multiple images, more sophisticated text)
  - -> three limitations, less effective downstream
- Limitation 1: text-to-image reference
  - rarely addressed in previous studies
  - intricate references: different words mention different images
  - e.g. question about multiple images (Fig. 1.c, Fig. 1.f); multiple images as exemplars, question about one image (Fig. 1.d)
  - web-crawled training data lacks explicit text-to-image references -> VLMs may fail
- Limitation 2: relationships between multiple images
  - spatial, temporal, logical relationships; understanding them helps handle queries
  - pre-training data from internet: weak connections between images, esp. far apart on same webpage
  - hampers understanding of relationships, limits reasoning
- Limitation 3: learning from in-context multi-modal demonstrations
  - pretrained LLMs benefit from few in-context demonstrations
  - VLM ICL limited: 1) BLIP-2, LLaVA only single-image prompts -> can't use multiple multi-modal demonstrations at inference
  - 2) Flamingo: multi-image inputs in pretraining, ICL emerges, but context schemes lack text-image references and closely related images -> limited ICL
  - no further supervised instruction tuning -> less effective on downstream tasks
- Our contributions
  - 1) MMICL: VLMs handle multi-modal inputs incl. relationships among images and text-to-image references
  - 2) new context scheme: extra image declaration section + image proxy tokens -> better ICL
  - 3) multi-modal ICL dataset built per scheme, adapted from existing datasets, supports training more capable VLMs
- Results
  - new SOTA on vision-language benchmarks incl. MME, MMBench
  - text-to-image references: 13-points improvement on Winoground (compositionality)
  - relationships among images: 12-points improvement on RAVEN (multi-image reasoning)
  - strong multi-modal ICL across tasks
  - mitigates language bias (VLMs ignore visual content with long textual context -> hallucinations)

steps.name: partial_draft
steps.text:
General-purpose vision-language pre-trained models (VLMs) have made big advances recently. Most recent VLMs add a visual encoder to a large language model (LLM), and they show impressive zero-shot capacities on many visual tasks. But LLMs can get rich background knowledge and task information from the prompt with in-context learning (ICL), while most VLMs still have trouble understanding complex multi-modal prompts that include multiple images. Previous studies mainly focus on user queries with a single image, and not on multi-modal prompts with multiple images and text interleaved. Some VLMs like Flamingo and Kosmos-1 can handle user queries with multiple images, but their pre-training data cannot give more sophisticated multi-modal prompts than interleaved image and text crawled from the web. So there is a gap between the prompts used for pre-training these VLMs and the user queries in real-world scenarios, which always have multiple images and more sophisticated text. Specifically, these VLMs may have the following three limitations, which make them less effective in downstream vision-language tasks.

Hard to Understand Text-to-Image Reference: Previous studies rarely try to address text-to-image reference in multi-modal prompts. But in user queries there are often intricate referential relationships between the text and the images, where different words mention different images. For example, the user may ask a specific question about multiple images (Fig. 1.c and Fig. 1.f), or use multiple images as exemplars and ask the question only about a specific image (Fig. 1.d). The training data used in previous studies is crawled from the web and may lack explicit text-to-image references. So VLMs might fail to handle user queries that involve intricate text-to-image references.

Hard to Understand the Relationships between Multiple Images: Multiple images often have spatial, temporal, and logical relationships between them, and if the model understands them correctly it can handle user queries better. But the pre-training data used by previous VLMs is collected from the internet and lacks close connections among images, especially when the images are far apart on the same webpage. This hampers the ability of VLMs to understand the intricate relationships among the images, and it further limits their reasoning ability.

- Limitation 3: learning from in-context multi-modal demonstrations
  - pretrained LLMs benefit from few in-context demonstrations
  - VLM ICL limited: 1) BLIP-2, LLaVA only single-image prompts -> can't use multiple multi-modal demonstrations at inference
  - 2) Flamingo: multi-image inputs in pretraining, ICL emerges, but context schemes lack text-image references and closely related images -> limited ICL
  - no further supervised instruction tuning -> less effective on downstream tasks
- Our contributions
  - 1) MMICL: VLMs handle multi-modal inputs incl. relationships among images and text-to-image references
  - 2) new context scheme: extra image declaration section + image proxy tokens -> better ICL
  - 3) multi-modal ICL dataset built per scheme, adapted from existing datasets, supports training more capable VLMs
- Results
  - new SOTA on vision-language benchmarks incl. MME, MMBench
  - text-to-image references: 13-points improvement on Winoground (compositionality)
  - relationships among images: 12-points improvement on RAVEN (multi-image reasoning)
  - strong multi-modal ICL across tasks
  - mitigates language bias (VLMs ignore visual content with long textual context -> hallucinations)

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
General-purpose vision-language pre-trained models (VLMs) have made big advances recently. Most recent VLMs add a visual encoder to a large language model (LLM), and they show impressive zero-shot capacities on many visual tasks. But LLMs can get rich background knowledge and task information from the prompt with in-context learning (ICL), while most VLMs still have trouble understanding complex multi-modal prompts that include multiple images. Previous studies mainly focus on user queries with a single image, and not on multi-modal prompts with multiple images and text interleaved. Some VLMs like Flamingo and Kosmos-1 can handle user queries with multiple images, but their pre-training data cannot give more sophisticated multi-modal prompts than interleaved image and text crawled from the web. So there is a gap between the prompts used for pre-training these VLMs and the user queries in real-world scenarios, which always have multiple images and more sophisticated text. Specifically, these VLMs may have the following three limitations, which make them less effective in downstream vision-language tasks.

Hard to Understand Text-to-Image Reference: Previous studies rarely try to address text-to-image reference in multi-modal prompts. But in user queries there are often intricate referential relationships between the text and the images, where different words mention different images. For example, the user may ask a specific question about multiple images (Fig. 1.c and Fig. 1.f), or use multiple images as exemplars and ask the question only about a specific image (Fig. 1.d). The training data used in previous studies is crawled from the web and may lack explicit text-to-image references. So VLMs might fail to handle user queries that involve intricate text-to-image references.

Hard to Understand the Relationships between Multiple Images: Multiple images often have spatial, temporal, and logical relationships between them, and if the model understands them correctly it can handle user queries better. But the pre-training data used by previous VLMs is collected from the internet and lacks close connections among images, especially when the images are far apart on the same webpage. This hampers the ability of VLMs to understand the intricate relationships among the images, and it further limits their reasoning ability.

Hard to Learn from In-Context Multi-Modal Demonstrations: Previous studies showed that pretrained LLMs can benefit from a few in-context demonstrations. But the ICL ability of current VLMs is quite limited. 1) VLMs like BLIP-2 and LLaVA only support multi-modal prompts with a single image, which hampers their ability to use multiple multi-modal demonstrations to improve their performance at inference. 2) VLMs such as Flamingo support multi-image inputs in pretraining and ICL abilities emerge, but their context schemes do not provide text-image references and closely related images. This stops them from giving sophisticated enough prompts to the VLMs, and so the effectiveness of their ICL ability is limited. Also, there is no further supervised instruction tuning, which hinders their effectiveness on downstream tasks.

In this paper we address these limitations. 1) We present MMICL, a new approach that lets VLMs deal with multi-modal inputs efficiently, including relationships among multiple images and text-to-image references. 2) We propose a new context scheme where an extra image declaration section is added, together with image proxy tokens, and this enhances the ICL ability of the VLM. 3) We build a multi-modal in-context learning dataset following the proposed scheme. The dataset is adapted from a range of existing datasets and can be used to support training more capable VLMs.

In our experiments MMICL gets new state-of-the-art performance on various vision-language benchmarks, including MME and MMBench. We also examine the three limitations we want to address, and MMICL shows exceptional ability in understanding text-to-image references (13-points improvement on Winoground, a vision-language compositionality benchmark) and intricate relationships among images (12-points improvement on RAVEN, a multi-image reasoning benchmark). MMICL also shows impressive multi-modal ICL performance across various tasks. We also see that MMICL efficiently mitigates the language bias, which often makes VLMs ignore the visual content when there is a lot of textual context, leading to hallucinations.

steps.text:

Some VLMs like Flamingo [6] and Kosmos-1 [7] can handle user queries with multiple images, but their pre-training data cannot give more sophisticated multi-modal prompts than interleaved image and text crawled from the web [8]. So there is a gap between the prompts used for pre-training these VLMs and the user queries in real-world scenarios, which always have multiple images and more sophisticated text. Specifically, these VLMs may have the following three limitations, which make them less effective in downstream vision-language tasks.

Hard to Understand Text-to-Image Reference: Previous studies rarely try to address text-to-image reference in multi-modal prompts. But in user queries there are often intricate referential relationships between the text and the images, where different words mention different images. For example, the user may ask a specific question about multiple images (Fig. 1.c and Fig. 1.f), or use multiple images as exemplars and ask the question only about a specific image (Fig. 1.d). The training data used in previous studies [2,6,9] is crawled from the web and may lack explicit text-to-image references. So VLMs might fail to handle user queries that involve intricate text-to-image references.

Hard to Understand the Relationships between Multiple Images: Multiple images often have spatial, temporal, and logical relationships between them, and if the model understands them correctly it can handle user queries better. But the pre-training data used by previous VLMs [6] is collected from the internet and lacks close connections among images, especially when the images are far apart on the same webpage. This hampers the ability of VLMs to understand the intricate relationships among the images, and it further limits their reasoning ability.

Hard to Learn from In-Context Multi-Modal Demonstrations: Previous studies showed that pretrained LLMs can benefit from a few in-context demonstrations [10,11]. But the ICL ability of current VLMs is quite limited. 1) VLMs like BLIP-2 [2] and LLaVA [5] only support multi-modal prompts with a single image, which hampers their ability to use multiple multi-modal demonstrations to improve their performance at inference. 2) VLMs such as Flamingo [6] support multi-image inputs in pretraining and ICL abilities emerge, but their context schemes do not provide text-image references and closely related images. This stops them from giving sophisticated enough prompts to the VLMs, and so the effectiveness of their ICL ability is limited. In this paper we address these limitations. 1) We present MMICL, a new approach that lets VLMs deal with multi-modal inputs efficiently, including relationships among multiple images and text-to-image references. 2) We propose a new context scheme where an extra image declaration section is added, together with image proxy tokens, and this enhances the ICL ability of the VLM. 3) We build a multi-modal in-context learning dataset following the proposed scheme. MMICL also shows impressive multi-modal ICL performance across various tasks. We also see that MMICL efficiently mitigates the language bias, which often makes VLMs ignore the visual content when there is a lot of textual context, leading to hallucinations.

steps.name: revised_draft
steps.text:
General-purpose vision-language pre-trained models (VLMs) have made significant advancements [1,2,3,4,5]. Recent VLMs mostly augment a large language model (LLM) with a visual encoder and show impressive zero-shot capacities in various visual tasks. However, unlike LLMs, which can extract rich background knowledge and task information from the prompt with in-context learning (ICL), most VLMs still struggle to understand complex multi-modal prompts that include multiple images. Previous studies [2,5] primarily focus on handling user queries with a single image rather than multi-modal prompts with interleaved multiple images and text. Although some VLMs like Flamingo [6] and Kosmos-1 [7] can handle user queries with multiple images, their pre-training data cannot provide more sophisticated multi-modal prompts than interleaved image and text crawled from the web [8]. Hence, there is a gap between the prompts used in pre-training these VLMs and the user queries in real-world scenarios, which always contain multiple images and more sophisticated text. Specifically, these VLMs may suffer from the following three limitations, which make them less effective in downstream vision-language tasks.

Hard to Understand Text-to-Image Reference: Previous studies rarely attempt to address the issue of text-to-image reference in multi-modal prompts. However, there are often intricate referential relationships between the text and images in user queries, with different words mentioning different images. For example, the user may ask a specific question about multiple images (Fig. 1.c and Fig. 1.f) or use multiple images as exemplars to ask the question only about a specific image (Fig. 1.d). However, the training data used in previous studies [2,6,9] is crawled from the web and may lack explicit text-to-image references. VLMs thus might fail to handle user queries involving intricate text-to-image references.

Hard to Understand the Relationships between Multiple Images: There are often spatial, temporal, and logical relationships between multiple images, and understanding them correctly allows the model to handle user queries better. However, the pre-training data used by previous VLMs [6] is collected from the internet and lacks close connections among images, especially when these images are far apart on the same webpage. This hampers the ability of VLMs to understand the intricate relationships among the images and further limits their reasoning ability.

Hard to Learn from In-Context Multi-Modal Demonstrations: Previous studies have shown that pretrained LLMs can benefit from a few in-context demonstrations [10,11]. However, the ICL ability of current VLMs is rather limited. Specifically: 1) VLMs like BLIP-2 [2] and LLaVA [5] only support multi-modal prompts with a single image, which hampers their ability to use multiple multi-modal demonstrations to enhance their performance during inference; 2) although VLMs such as Flamingo [6] support multi-image inputs during pretraining and ICL abilities emerge, their context schemes fail to provide text-image references and closely related images. This inhibits them from offering sophisticated enough prompts to the VLMs, thereby limiting the effectiveness of their ICL ability. Besides, the lack of further supervised instruction tuning hinders their effectiveness across downstream tasks.

In this paper, to address the aforementioned limitations: 1) We present MMICL, a new approach that allows VLMs to efficiently deal with multi-modal inputs, including relationships among multiple images and text-to-image references. 2) We propose a novel context scheme in which an extra image declaration section, along with image proxy tokens, enhances the ICL ability of the VLM. 3) We construct a multi-modal in-context learning dataset in accordance with the proposed scheme. The dataset is adapted from a range of existing datasets and can be used to support the training of more capable VLMs.

Our experiments show that MMICL achieves new state-of-the-art performance on various vision-language benchmarks, including MME [12] and MMBench [13]. Comprehensive examinations of the three limitations we aim to address show that MMICL has exceptional ability in understanding text-to-image references (13-points improvement on the vision-language compositionality benchmark, Winoground [14]) and intricate relationships among images (12-points improvement on the multi-image reasoning benchmark, RAVEN [9]). Moreover, MMICL demonstrates impressive multi-modal ICL performance across various tasks. We also observe that MMICL efficiently mitigates the language bias, which often causes VLMs to ignore visual content when facing extensive textual contexts, leading to hallucinations.
